identity.title: exoALMA. VIII. Probabilistic Moment Maps and Data Products Using Nonparametric Linear Models

paper_type_evidence.quote: In this paper we develop a flexible linear model of the intensity distribution in each frequency channel, accounting for spatial correlations from the point spread function.
We perform all analysis using the fiducial $^{12}$CO $J=3-2$ cubes (cite: Teague_exoALMA) for HD 135344B, MWC 758, CQ Tau and J1842.

question.value: Can a non-parametric linear model of per-channel intensity, with beam-correlated noise, give probabilistic moment maps and disk-fit uncertainties that are debiased from beam smearing?

evidence.quote: Our method debiases peak intensity, peak velocity, and line width maps, particularly in disk substructures that are only partially resolved.
We find that uncertainties in stellar mass and inclination increase by an order of magnitude due to the more realistic noise model.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2021.1.01123.L.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit the non-parametric linear model per channel and draw posterior cube samples

method.value: Each channel is modelled independently as a Fourier-series intensity map convolved with the beam, with beam-correlated Gaussian noise and a smoothness-promoting Gaussian prior; the posterior mean and covariance are analytic; 100 posterior cube samples are drawn

evidence.quote: has an analytic form thanks to the linearity of the model, and because both the noise and prior are normal distributions
yielding 100 model cube samples, both before and after beam convolution.
We somewhat arbitrarily choose values for the hyperparameters of $\lambda=s=0.1$, since we found them to be performant in terms of predicting the data

key_parameters.value: number of basis functions per axis = 1.25 x pixels per axis (over-parameterised)

evidence.quote: We set the number of basis functions in each direction $p_x, p_y$ to be 1.25 times the number of pixels in each direction $n_x, n_y$, rounded to the nearest integer.

key_parameters.value: same noise sigma for all pixels, from the standard deviation in channels with no significant signal

evidence.quote: we assume the same $\sigma$ for all pixels in the cube, which we estimate from the standard deviation of the data in channels with no significant signal.

key_parameters.value: L = 3, pixel coordinates uniformly spaced between 0 and 1

evidence.quote: We choose spatial coordinates $x_i,y_i$ for the pixels uniformly spaced between 0 and 1, and set $L=3$ following (cite: hoggvillar).

key_parameters.value: numpy lstsq with RCOND = 1e-16 instead of explicit inverses

evidence.quote: with RCOND set to $10^{-16}$ to zero out small eigenvalues near machine precision

assumptions.value: Gaussian beam kernel (circular, FWHM 0.15 arcsec) and noise correlated on the scale of the beam; uv sampling not modelled

evidence.quote: Let $h(x,y)$ be a function representing the kernel of the beam, a circular 2D gaussian
We assume that the noise is spatially correlated on the scale of the beam

fitting.value: Analytic Gaussian posterior (generalised least squares with Gaussian prior, mean zero, feature-weighted variances); samples drawn via Cholesky or spectral decomposition of the covariance

evidence.quote: We choose a prior that penalises high frequency basis functions more than low frequency ones, in order to encourage smoothness.
If $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}$ is positive definite then we use a Cholesky decomposition

analysis_steps.goal: Combine cube samples with DISCMINER for J1842

method.value: Draw 30 beam-convolved cube samples, fit each with DISCMINER, then aggregate all DISCMINER posterior samples into a combined posterior; compare with DISCMINER on the data directly and with the production exoALMA fit

evidence.quote: We fit each cube sample with DISCMINER, obtaining many posterior distributions, where each is conditioned on a single cube sample.
Finally, we estimate the combined posterior by aggregating the posterior DISCMINER samples from all fits.
